title: Count Complete Substrings
summary: Given a string and an integer k, count the number of substrings where each character appears exactly k times and the difference between any two adjacent characters is at most 2.
statement: Given a string and an integer k, count the number of substrings where each character appears exactly k times and the difference between any two adjacent characters is at most 2.
constraints: A complete substring has every distinct character exactly k times.
Every adjacent character pair in it differs by at most two alphabet positions; count all complete substrings.
hints: The adjacency rule partitions the word into independent maximal segments.
Within one segment, a complete substring with d distinct letters has fixed length d*k.
For every d from one to 26, slide that width and test exact counts; sum across segments.
Every valid substring lies wholly in one segment and appears in exactly the window size matching its distinct-character count.
editorial: Every valid substring lies wholly in one segment and appears in exactly the window size matching its distinct-character count.

tests.explanation: Three substrings satisfy both exact frequencies and the adjacent-letter distance rule.
Each constant block and compatible combined blocks are checked by frequency windows.
